IDs are short business codes (K1, K1a, P1, L1), not surrogate ints/GUIDs.
12	- (constraint) Brownfield scaffold has exactly one backend project (seed-b-backend.Api) and one test project — no Domain/Application/Infrastructure class libraries exist. Spine must ratify this single-project shape, not invent a multi-project split.
13	- (assumption) Inherit PRD assumptions verbatim (not re-decided here): EUR currency; page size 20; default sort name-asc; price sort = min offer price; substring case-insensitive search; property filters require a chosen subcategory; avg rating rounded to 1 decimal; no view-count dedup; author-name overwrite semantics for ratings; delivery/contact fields = name+address+email; order access via confirmation page/link, no account-bound history (OQ-1 open); fixed single order status 'Eingegangen'.
14	- (direction) Paradigm: Layered architecture (n-tier) inside the single existing ASP.NET Core project, paired with a separate Angular SPA over REST/JSON. Server-authoritative: no auth exists, so every trust-sensitive rule (price freeze, order validation, rating upsert, view counter) must live in backend Services, never trusted to the client.
15	- (decision) AD-1 Backend internal layering & dependency direction: single seed-b-backend.Api project layered by folder — Controllers (HTTP only, map DTO<->Service) -> Services (all business rules) -> Data (EF Core entities/DbContext/Migrations/startup seeding). Controllers never touch DbContext directly; Data is never referenced by the frontend. Binds: all backend FRs. Prevents: ad-hoc splitting into extra class-library projects, or business rules leaking into Controllers/entities, causing two stories to structure the backend incompatibly.
16	- (decision) AD-2 English identifiers, German UI text: all code identifiers (C# classes/EF entities, TS interfaces, API routes) use English nouns (Product, Category, Subcategory, Supplier, Offer, Order, OrderItem, Rating, Cart-is-client-only-see-AD4); user-facing text stays German per document_output_language. Fixed glossary mapping: Produkt=Product, Kategorie=Category, Unterkategorie=Subcategory, Eigenschaft=Attribute, Lieferant=Supplier, Angebot=Offer, Warenkorb(-position)=Cart(Item, client-side), Bestellung/-position=Order/OrderItem, Bewertung=Rating, Aufrufzähler=ViewCount. Binds: all entities/DTOs/routes. Prevents: one story naming Produkt.cs and another Product.cs / mixed-language routes.
17	- (decision) AD-3 ID strategy: seed-origin reference entities (Category, Subcategory, Supplier, Product, Offer) keep the seed's string business codes as primary key (matches anfangsdatenbestand.json ids 1:1, no id-remapping during seeding). Entities created at runtime (Order, OrderItem, Rating) use server-generated GUID keys. Binds: FR-16 seeding, FR-13/14 order, FR-10 rating. Prevents: one builder giving Product an int identity PK (breaking idempotent seeding by natural key) while another keeps string codes.
18	- (decision) AD-4 Cart is client-side-only state: no server-side Cart/CartItem entity, table, or anonymous-session identity of any kind. The Angular app holds cart lines {productId, offerId/supplierId, quantity} in memory + browser localStorage. Justification: FR-12 already requires the cart to always show the CURRENT live offer price (not a price captured at add-time), so a server-persisted cart would just be a second, potentially-stale copy of frontend state; checkout submits the whole cart content in one request to POST /api/orders. Binds: FR-11, FR-12, FR-13. Prevents: inventing a server session/cookie mechanism that duplicates and can drift from client state, and resolves the PRD's open 'anonymous session mechanism' ASSUMPTION by making it unnecessary.
19	- (decision) AD-5 Order-time full snapshot: OrderItem stores a complete denormalized copy at creation (product name, supplier name, unit price, quantity) — never a live join back to Product/Offer. Binds: FR-13, FR-14. Prevents: any code path that re-derives an order line's displayed price/name from current catalog state, which would silently violate the price-freeze guarantee if a supplier later changes its price or the catalog is reseeded.
20	- (decision) AD-6 Atomic order validation: POST /api/orders validates the ENTIRE submitted cart (non-empty; every quantity is a positive integer; every referenced product+supplier Offer still exists) inside one service method/DB transaction BEFORE writing any Order/OrderItem row. Any single violation rejects the whole request (ProblemDetails, see AD-12) with zero rows persisted; there is no per-line partial acceptance. Order retrieval after creation is by the returned OrderId only (confirmation page / direct link) — no listing/search endpoint, per PRD OQ-1 assumption. Binds: FR-13, FR-14, FR-15. Prevents: an implementation that loops over cart lines and best-effort-inserts valid ones.
21	- (decision) AD-7 Category-specific attributes: Product.Attributes stored as one JSON column matching the seed's per-product eigenschaften object 1:1 (typed scalars: string/bool/number/null). Subcategory owns the attribute-name schema (list of names, from seed unterkategorien[].eigenschaften) in its own small table/collection. Filtering (FR-6) does exact-match equality against JSON_VALUE per requested attribute, AND-combined across attributes. [ASSUMPTION: equality compares the JSON scalar as text for all value types incl. bool/number — sufficient at this project's scale (14 seed products), no type-aware indexing]. Binds: FR-6, FR-8, FR-16. Prevents: an EAV-table design in one story and a flat-columns design in another producing incompatible schemas/filter queries; rejected alternative EAV table logged here for traceability.
22	- (decision) AD-8 Rating integrity: a unique DB constraint on (ProductId, AuthorName) backs an upsert (update-if-exists else insert) for FR-10 — never check-then-insert at the app layer alone. Average rating and rating count are always computed at READ time via an aggregation query over Rating rows, never stored/cached as denormalized columns on Product. Binds: FR-10, FR-8. Prevents: a stale denormalized average drifting from the underlying Rating rows if an update path is missed.
23	- (decision) AD-9 View counter: Product.ViewCount is a persisted column, incremented via a single atomic UPDATE ... SET ViewCount = ViewCount + 1 (SQL-side increment) on every product-detail GET, never a read-modify-write from the app layer. Binds: FR-9, FR-7. Prevents: lost updates under concurrent detail requests to the same product, and confirms the NFR that the counter is durable (survives restart), matching the seed-load idempotency guarantee of AD-13.
24	- (decision) AD-10 Server-side-only list querying: category/subcategory scope, full-text search, attribute filters, sort (name/price/popularity) and pagination all execute as ONE server-side query pipeline in the Product Service; the API always returns the already-filtered/sorted/paged page plus total count. The Angular client never locally re-filters, re-sorts, or re-paginates a result set it already has. Binds: FR-1 through FR-7. Prevents: a frontend feature quietly re-sorting a page client-side and disagreeing with the backend's page/total-count metadata.
25	- (decision) AD-11 Money as decimal end-to-end: all prices and sums use C# decimal / SQL decimal(18,2); float/double are never used for currency anywhere in the stack (backend, DTOs, or the Angular layer doing display formatting). Binds: FR-4 (price sort), FR-8, FR-9/12/13/14 totals. Prevents: floating-point rounding drift between cart-total, order-total, and per-line displays computed in different places.

Binds: all endpoints. Prevents: each controller inventing its own ad-hoc error JSON shape.

Binds: FR-16. Prevents: relying on EnsureCreated (skips migrations) or an ad-hoc seed check scattered across multiple entry points that could reseed/duplicate data.
28	- (decision) AD-14 Angular structure: standalone components only (no NgModules, matching Angular 22 default scaffold), feature-folder layout (core/ for shared http services+models, features/catalog, features/product-detail, features/cart, features/checkout), Angular signals for local reactive state (cart, filters). (`seed-b-frontend/package.json`, `seed-b-frontend/angular.json`, `seed-b-backend.Api/seed-b-backend.Api.csproj`,
`seed-b-backend.Tests/seed-b-backend.Tests.csproj`). Every claim below is checked against those files where
possible; where the repo has no independent artifact to check against, that is stated explicitly rather than
asserted as fact.

Note: the spine's own `.memlog.md` already logs this exact gap ("No web-search tool available... stack versions
taken as given from addendum/scaffold... Logged as a gap for the reviewer's version-verification lens"), so the
architect flagged the limitation proactively. This review confirms that flag is warranted and sharpens exactly
which line items it applies to.

## 1. Angular 22.1 / TypeScript 6.0 / Node 24.19 LTS

- **Angular 22.1**: `seed-b-frontend/package.json` pins `@angular/core` etc. to `^22.1.0` and
  `@angular/build`/`@angular/cli` to `^22.1.3`. **Matches the spine exactly.**
- **TypeScript 6.0**: `package.json` pins `typescript: ~6.0.2`. **Matches the spine** ("TypeScript 6.0" — the
  scaffold's exact pin is a patch version within that line).
- **npm 11.17.0**: `package.json` has `"packageManager": "npm@11.17.0"`. **Matches the spine's parenthetical
  exactly.**
- **Node.js 24.19 LTS**: **not independently verifiable against the repo.** There is no `.nvmrc`, no `engines`
  field in `package.json`, no `global.json`-equivalent, no Dockerfile, and no CI config anywhere in the repo that
  pins a Node version. The only source for "24.19 LTS" is the PRD addendum's mandated-stack text

- **Plausibility (reasoning only, not a web-verified fact)**: Node's even-numbered-year LTS cadence (18→Oct 2022,
  20→Oct 2023, 22→Oct 2024, 24→Oct 2025) makes "Node 24 as LTS" by August 2026 timing-plausible. However, a minor
  version of `.19` roughly ~10 months after LTS promotion implies close to two minor releases per month, which is
  faster than Node's typical ~monthly minor cadence for an LTS line (compare: Node 20 was around `20.16`–`20.17`
  roughly 10-11 months after its Oct-2023 LTS promotion). `24.19` is not impossible but is on the high side of what
  the historical cadence would predict. This is a plausibility judgment, not a confirmed error — flag it as
  unverified, don't treat it as fabricated.

## 2. ASP.NET Core 10.0 / C# 14 / .NET 10.0 / EF Core 10.0.11

- **.NET 10.0 / ASP.NET Core 10.0**: `seed-b-backend.Api.csproj` has `<TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>`

  exactly**, including the specific patch version the spine cites. The spine's own phrasing ("as pinned in

  independently web-verified fact.

This is a real, long-standing capability, not a fabricated one:

- SQL Server has shipped `JSON_VALUE`, `JSON_QUERY`, `ISJSON`, and `OPENJSON` since SQL Server 2016, usable against
  JSON stored in an `nvarchar`/`nvarchar(max)` column (SQL Server has historically not had a distinct native JSON
  storage type prior to very recent versions — JSON is stored as text and validated/queried via these functions).
  Filtering with `JSON_VALUE(column, '$.path') = @value` is a standard, well-documented pattern.
- EF Core has supported mapping to/from JSON columns (owned-entity-as-JSON, `ToJson()`) since EF Core 7, with the
  capability maturing through EF 8/9, and EF Core 10 (per the pinned `10.0.11`) continues to support it. Combining
  EF's JSON column mapping with a raw/translated `JSON_VALUE` predicate for filtering is realistic and something
  EF Core's SQL Server provider is capable of translating or that can be done via raw SQL/`EF.Functions`.
- The spine's own caveat — that equality compares the JSON scalar as text across all value types (string/bool/
  number), with no type-aware indexing, and that this is "sufficient at this project's scale (14 seed products)"
  — is an honest, load-bearing caveat rather than an overclaim. It correctly frames this as a scale-appropriate
  simplification, not a claim that `JSON_VALUE` does type-aware comparison natively.
- **Verdict: AD-7's technical premise is sound and not fabricated.** No correction needed here. (I cannot
  web-verify SQL Server's exact current feature set as of mid-2026 — e.g., whether a native JSON data type has
  since shipped and would be a better fit than `nvarchar`+`JSON_VALUE` — but the pattern the spine describes is
  real regardless of what else may additionally exist by now, so this is not a case of asserting something
  false.)

Ranked by how load-bearing / how little repo corroboration exists:

1. **Node.js "24.19 LTS"** — the single Stack-table entry with *no* corroborating file anywhere in the repo (no

2. **C# 14** — inferred from `.NET 10.0`/`net10.0` TargetFramework rather than stated anywhere in the csproj files
   (no `<LangVersion>` set). Reasonable inference, but not a repo-confirmed fact the way `.NET 10.0` and
   `EF Core 10.0.11` are.
3. **TypeScript 6.0 / Angular 22.1 / Node 24 as real, currently-shipping major versions as of mid-2026** — these
   match the scaffold's own pins exactly, so internally the spine is *consistent*, but "internally consistent
   with the scaffold" is a different claim than "these version numbers correspond to real releases that exist in
   the world on 2026-08-17." Since the scaffold itself was presumably generated/seeded with the same
   no-web-access constraint, matching it doesn't independently establish real-world existence — it only proves
   spine-and-scaffold agree with each other. This distinction is worth being explicit about in the memlog: "spine
   matches scaffold" ≠ "scaffold versions were externally verified."
4. **Microsoft SQL Server version** — the spine correctly avoids asserting a specific version here ("supplied at

| 1a | Angular 22.1 | Yes (`package.json`) | Match |
| 1b | TypeScript 6.0 | Yes (`package.json`) | Match |

# Reconciliation Review: ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md vs. PRD + Addendum

**Scope:** ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md (2026-08-17 draft) reconciled against `prd.md` and `addendum.md` for the Online-Handel Webshop, plus a direct check of `seed-b-backend.Api/Data/anfangsdatenbestand.json` against the spine's AD-3/AD-7 claims.

**Overall verdict:** The spine is largely faithful and unusually disciplined about honoring PRD assumptions (cart-as-localStorage, order-by-confirmation-link, no-caps, no admin area are all correctly carried through and even cross-referenced to the right OQ/§5 items). However it has one factual inaccuracy against the actual seed file (AD-3's Offer claim), one structural gap where an entire entity's attribute shape (Order's own fields) is never described by any AD despite two PRD assumptions pinning that shape, and several PRD `[ASSUMPTION]` tags with real architectural consequences (price-sort semantics, Offer uniqueness, two-level category cap) that are silently left un-governed rather than being honored or explicitly flagged as diverged.

---

## HIGH — factual / structural gaps

### H1. AD-3's ID-strategy claim about `Offer` does not match the actual seed file

AD-3 states: *"`Category`, `Subcategory`, `Supplier`, `Product`, `Offer` keep the seed's string business codes (`"K1"`, `"K1a"`, `"P1"`, `"L1"`, ...) as primary key, unchanged from `anfangsdatenbestand.json`."*

Checked against `seed-b-backend.Api/Data/anfangsdatenbestand.json`: `kategorien[]`, `unterkategorien[]`, `lieferanten[]`, and `produkte[]` all carry an explicit `"id"` field ("K1", "K1a", "L1", "P1", ...). **`angebote[]` do not** — each offer is an anonymous nested object `{ "lieferantId": "...", "preis": ... }` inside a product, with no `id`/code field of its own anywhere in the file. AD-3 lumps `Offer` in with the four entities that genuinely have seed string codes, but there is no such code to reuse for `Offer`. The correct natural key for `Offer` is the composite `(ProductId, SupplierId)` — the addendum's own line ("Angebot: die Kombination aus Produkt, Lieferant und ... Preis") and the PRD glossary ("derselbe Lieferant führt ein Produkt höchstens einmal") both point at a composite key, not a standalone code. As written, a story-writer following AD-3 literally would look for an `Offer.Id` seed value that doesn't exist.

**Fix direction:** AD-3 should either drop `Offer` from the "keeps seed string code" list and state its actual key strategy (composite `(ProductId, SupplierId)`, or a server-generated surrogate GUID/int with a unique index on that composite), or explicitly note that `Offer` is the one exception among the seed-sourced entities.

### H2. `Order`'s own attribute shape (delivery/contact fields, status) is never described by any AD

Two PRD `[ASSUMPTION]` tags concretely pin what `Order` itself must carry:

- FR-13 Konsequenzen: *"Erfasste Liefer- und Kontaktdaten umfassen mindestens Name, Lieferadresse (Straße/Hausnummer, PLZ, Ort, Land) und E-Mail-Adresse `[ASSUMPTION: konkrete Feldliste nicht im Auftrag spezifiziert]`."*
- FR-14 Konsequenzen: *"Der angezeigte Status ist der bei Anlage vergebene Wert `[ASSUMPTION: Bestellungen erhalten bei Anlage einen einzigen festen Status ("Eingegangen"); Statusänderungen sind nicht Teil dieses Auftrags...]`."*

AD-5 ("Order-time full snapshot") only specifies what `OrderItem` stores (product name, supplier name, unit price, quantity) — it says nothing about `Order`'s own fields. No other AD, the ERD (`ORDER ||--|{ ORDER_ITEM : contains`, no attributes listed), or the DTOs bullet in the folder-structure sketch mentions delivery address, contact fields, or a status field/value at all. This is exactly the kind of testable, PRD-flagged consequence the AD-list format is supposed to catch, and it's missing entirely — not diverged-from-with-a-flag, just absent. A downstream epic/story writer has no spine-level anchor for either the field list or the fixed-status behavior (including the important negative constraint that status has no transitions, tied to the explicit Non-Goal "kein Verwaltungsbereich ... Bestellstatus in dieser Version keine Übergänge kennt").

**Fix direction:** Add an AD (or extend AD-5) that pins `Order`'s own field set — delivery/contact fields per the FR-13 assumption, and a `Status` field fixed to a single value at creation with no transition mechanism, per the FR-14 assumption and the §5 non-goal.

### H3. No uniqueness constraint stated for `Offer(ProductId, SupplierId)`

PRD Glossary: *"Ein Produkt kann mehrere Angebote unterschiedlicher Lieferanten haben; derselbe Lieferant führt ein Produkt höchstens einmal."* This is a real integrity constraint (at most one offer per product+supplier pair) with the same shape as the one AD-8 explicitly enforces for `Rating` (unique constraint on `(ProductId, AuthorName)` backing an upsert). No equivalent AD exists for `Offer`. Combined with H1 (no defined PK for `Offer`), this leaves `Offer`'s entire identity/integrity story ungoverned — nothing in the spine would catch a future migration that lets the same supplier list a product twice.

---

## MEDIUM — PRD assumptions with real design consequences, left un-governed

### M1. FR-4's price-sort semantics (which price, when a product has several) is never pinned by an AD

FR-4 Konsequenzen carries `[ASSUMPTION: da ein Produkt mehrere Angebotspreise hat, referenziert die Preis-Sortierung den niedrigsten aktuell gültigen Angebotspreis]` — i.e., sort-by-price must use `MIN(Offer.Price)` per product, not average or first-found. AD-10 ("Server-side-only list querying") lists "sort (name/price/popularity)" as part of the one query pipeline but never states what "price" resolves to for a multi-offer product. This is a genuine query-design decision (requires a grouped/correlated subquery over `Offer`) that two different stories could resolve differently (min vs. avg vs. "any") without contradicting anything currently written in the spine.

### M2. AD-10's own wording for FR-5 risks the opposite of what the PRD assumes

FR-5's assumption is explicit: *"einfache Teilstring-Suche ohne Relevanz-Ranking oder Fuzzy-Matching"*. AD-10 describes this capability using the phrase "full-text search," which on the pinned stack (SQL Server + EF Core) is also the name of a real, distinct feature (`CONTAINS`/`FREETEXT`, relevance-ranked, fuzzy-capable). A story-writer reading AD-10's literal words could reach for SQL Server Full-Text Search and get ranking/fuzzy behavior the PRD explicitly rules out. Not a contradiction of intent (the spine clearly means plain substring `LIKE`), but the terminology itself is a foot-gun the spine should avoid, given how central "don't use the loaded term" would be to keeping this AD-list from being misread.

### M3. The PRD's explicit "exactly two levels, not just up to two" non-goal has no corresponding architectural invariant

§5 Non-Goals: *"Kategorien mit mehr als zwei Ebenen — die Hierarchie ist strukturell auf zwei Ebenen begrenzt, nicht nur 'bis zu zwei'."* The PRD deliberately calls out that this is a *structural* cap, not a soft convention. The spine's ERD models `Category ||--o{ Subcategory` with no further nesting, which is consistent, but no AD states this as an invariant the way AD-1 pins the layering direction. Nothing would stop a later story from adding a self-referencing `ParentCategoryId` to `Category` "for future extensibility," which the PRD explicitly forbids.

### M4. FR-1's page-size and FR-4's default-sort assumptions are never mentioned anywhere in the spine

FR-1: `[ASSUMPTION: Seitengröße = 20 Produkte je Seite]`. FR-4: `[ASSUMPTION: Standardsortierung = Name aufsteigend]`. AD-10 covers the pagination/sort *mechanism* but neither concrete value appears anywhere in the spine (searched full text — no "20", no default-sort statement). These are lower-altitude than M1–M3 (arguably config, not architecture), but per the PRD's own Assumptions Index they are tracked as assumptions with testable consequences (FR-1's "fixed page size, no padding on last page"), and the spine neither honors them explicitly nor flags a divergence.

---

## LOW — narrower, more implementation-adjacent gaps

### L1. FR-11's cart-merge behavior isn't governed by any AD

FR-11 Konsequenzen: `[ASSUMPTION: Wird dasselbe Produkt beim selben Lieferanten erneut hinzugefügt, wird die Menge der bestehenden Position erhöht statt eine doppelte Position anzulegen]`. AD-4 describes the cart's storage shape (`productId`, `offerId`/`supplierId`, `quantity` in signals + localStorage) but not this specific dedup-by-increment rule. Since AD-4 already delegates all cart logic to the frontend with no backend governance, this is a minor omission rather than a risk of drift between layers — but it's still a testable FR consequence with zero spine coverage.

### L2. FR-8's rating-rounding assumption isn't mentioned by AD-8

FR-8: `[ASSUMPTION: Durchschnittsbewertung wird auf eine Nachkommastelle gerundet dargestellt]`. AD-8 pins the *computation* (read-time aggregation, never denormalized) but not the *display* rounding. # Reviewer Gate — Rubric Review

**Target:** `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/architecture/architecture-bmad-core-bmm-2026-08-17/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md`
**Reviewed against:** `prd.md` + `addendum.md` (same directory tree) and the actual code scaffold (`seed-b-backend.Api/`, `seed-b-backend.Tests/`, `seed-b-frontend/`).
**Date:** 2026-08-17

## Verdict

**Conditional pass** — the spine is well-structured, its layering/paradigm choices genuinely ratify the existing scaffold, and it covers all 5 PRD feature areas. However it contains one significant internal-consistency defect (Offer's identity/PK is asserted three different, mutually incompatible ways across AD-3/AD-4/AD-6) that is exactly the kind of divergence risk this document exists to close, plus a documentation/traceability error in the Capability Map and an unresolvable-as-written cross-stack rule (AD-11 for the Angular side). Recommend fixing these before treating the spine as build-ready.

---

## Findings

### 1. [HIGH] AD-3's claim that `Offer` has a "seed's string business code" primary key is factually wrong and contradicts AD-4/AD-6 — real divergence risk

**Checklist items:** #1 (fixes real divergence points), #2 (Rule enforceability/logical soundness)

AD-3 states:

> `Category`, `Subcategory`, `Supplier`, `Product`, `Offer` keep the seed's string business codes (`"K1"`, `"K1a"`, `"P1"`, `"L1"`, ...) as primary key, unchanged from `anfangsdatenbestand.json`.

Verified against the actual seed file (`seed-b-backend.Api/Data/anfangsdatenbestand.json`): every `angebot` (offer) entry is `{"lieferantId": "L1", "preis": 29.99}` — **no `id` field exists anywhere in any offer object**, in any product. (Confirmed programmatically: `any offer has id field: False`.) The four example codes AD-3 gives (`K1`, `K1a`, `P1`, `L1`) map exactly to Category/Subcategory/Product/Supplier — tellingly, no offer-code example is given, because none exists in the source data.

This is not a cosmetic gap — the spine is internally inconsistent about how `Offer` is identified:
- **AD-3** implies `Offer` gets a single natural string-code PK "unchanged from" the seed, like the other four entities.
- **AD-4** (cart line shape) hedges with `offerId`**/**`supplierId` — the slash is the tell that the author wasn't sure which one exists.
- **AD-6** (order validation) treats offer identity as a **composite** `(product, supplier)` pair ("every referenced product+supplier `Offer` still exists"), not a singular code.

A future epic/story breakdown building on this spine has no single answer to "what is `Offer.Id`, and what does the client send to reference an offer — a synthetic PK, or `(productId, supplierId)`?" Two independent stories (e.g. the catalog/detail story emitting offers, and the cart/checkout story consuming them) could genuinely diverge here: one could invent a surrogate GUID/composite string per offer, another could carry `(productId, supplierId)` end-to-end with no `Offer` PK at all. This is precisely the class of "divergence point for the level below" the spine's own Prevents-clauses are meant to close, and it isn't closed.

**Recommendation:** AD-3 should explicitly state that `Offer` has **no natural seed PK**; either give it a composite key `(ProductId, SupplierId)` (consistent with AD-6's own phrasing and with the PRD glossary: "derselbe Lieferant führt ein Produkt höchstens einmal" — i.e., the pair is already unique) or a server-generated surrogate key, and then make AD-4's cart-line shape consistent with that choice (drop the `offerId/supplierId` hedge).

---

### 2. [MEDIUM] Capability → Architecture Map row for 4.2 cites AD-5, which has no relationship to FR-8/FR-9/FR-10

**Checklist item:** #6 (covers PRD's 5 feature areas correctly), #2 (traceability accuracy)

The map row reads:

> `4.2 Produktdetail & Bewertungen (FR-8..FR-10) | Services/ProductService, Services/RatingService, features/product-detail | AD-5, AD-8, AD-9, AD-11`

But AD-5 ("Order-time full snapshot") explicitly declares `**Binds:** FR-13, FR-14` — it governs `OrderItem` denormalization at order time, and has no logical connection to the product-detail/rating capability (FR-8–FR-10). AD-5 correctly appears in the 4.4 (Bestellung) row instead. This looks like a copy/paste or mapping error. It's a traceability defect, not a structural one, but a builder skimming the map to find "what governs product detail" would be pointed at the wrong AD (and could plausibly miss that AD-7, which *is* relevant to displaying a product's `Attributes`/`Eigenschaften` on the detail page, isn't cross-listed here either — it's only listed under 4.1).

**Recommendation:** Remove AD-5 from the 4.2 row; consider adding AD-7 (attributes) since the detail view also renders category-specific attributes.

---

### 3. [MEDIUM] AD-11's "decimal everywhere including Angular display formatting" rule is not achievable as literally stated on the TypeScript side

**Checklist item:** #2 (Rule must logically prevent the stated divergence)

AD-11's Rule: "all prices and sums use C# `decimal` / SQL `decimal(18,2)`. `float`/`double` are never used for currency, anywhere in the stack **including Angular display formatting**."

TypeScript/JavaScript has no native decimal type — every JS number, including ones typed `number` in TS, is an IEEE-754 double. The rule bans float/double for currency "anywhere in the stack" but doesn't say what replaces it client-side (a decimal library such as `decimal.js`/`big.js`, integer-cents arithmetic, or "plain JS number is acceptable as long as summation/display is rounded to 2dp"). Given AD-4 puts cart totals under the plain Angular signal store (`quantity * currentOfferPrice`, summed across multiple lines), this is exactly the place cumulative float rounding drift (the very failure mode AD-11 exists to prevent) could occur, and the spine gives no concrete guardrail for it. As written, this AD cannot be mechanically satisfied by a frontend builder — it will either be silently ignored (native JS numbers used anyway) or produce two different fixes across stories (one adds a decimal library, another just formats with `toFixed(2)`).

**Recommendation:** Either scope AD-11's cross-stack claim down to "backend-authoritative calculations only (client-side arithmetic is display convenience, re-validated server-side per AD-6)" — which is arguably already true and sufficient — or name a specific client-side approach (e.g., "cart/order totals summed as integer cents in TS, converted only for display").

---

### 4. [LOW] AD-1's Rule only partially covers its own stated Prevents-clause

**Checklist item:** #2

Prevents-clause: "business rules leaking into Controllers or EF entities...". Rule: "Controllers never construct or query `DbContext` directly — only Services do." This technical guardrail stops one specific failure mode (direct DB access from a Controller) but does not stop a Controller from containing business logic that doesn't touch `DbContext` (e.g., computing a rejection reason or re-deriving a total from Service-returned data inside the controller method body). The Rule is a necessary but not sufficient control for the Prevents-clause as worded. Low severity because this is a common, pragmatic simplification in architecture docs and the folder/dependency-direction convention still does most of the work — flagging for completeness only.

---

### 5. [LOW] Logging/observability is a silent dimension, not clearly bucketed under the existing Deferred item

**Checklist item:** #8 (structural dimensions the initiative altitude should own)

The Deferred section explicitly and correctly addresses the operational/environmental envelope: "Deployment, containerization, operations — explicit addendum non-goal; only the runtime contract (`ConnectionStrings__Default` env var) is fixed, nothing about hosting/infra/CI." This satisfies the letter of checklist item 8. However, application-level logging/observability (structured logging, error tracking, correlation of a rejected-order ProblemDetails response back to server logs) is never mentioned anywhere in the spine, including in Deferred — it's ambiguous whether it's meant to be swept into "operations" or was simply not considered. Given the project's small scope this is plausibly fine to leave fully silent, but per the rubric a wholly-silent dimension is technically a finding even if low-risk here.

**Recommendation:** One sentence in Deferred ("application logging: rely on ASP.NET Core default console logging, no structured/external logging pipeline — out of scope") would close this cheaply.

---

## Checklist-by-checklist summary

| # | Check | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fixes real divergence points for the level below | **Partial** — misses the Offer-identity divergence (Finding 1) |
| 2 | Every AD's Rule is enforceable and logically prevents its Prevents-clause | **Partial** — AD-3 self-contradicts (Finding 1); AD-11 unenforceable as stated on the frontend (Finding 3); AD-1 partially covers its Prevents-clause (Finding 4) |
| 3 | Nothing under Deferred lets independent builders diverge incompatibly | **Pass** — reviewed all 9 Deferred bullets individually; each is either a pure omission (additive later) or a already-resolved non-goal, none creates an incompatible-schema risk |
| 4 | Named tech (Stack table) is plausible/current | **Pass** — every entry cross-checked against the actual `.csproj`/`package.json` in the scaffold (Angular ^22.1.0, TS ~6.0.2, net10.0, EF Core SqlServer 10.0.11, xunit.v3 3.2.2, vitest ^4.0.8) and matches exactly; nothing invented |
| 5 | Ratifies rather than contradicts the brownfield scaffold | **Pass** — AD-1 (single-project, folder-layered) matches `seed-b-backend.Api.csproj`/`Program.cs` (single Web SDK project, no extra class libraries yet); AD-14 (standalone components) matches `app.ts` (`@Component({ imports: [...] })`, no NgModule) and `app.config.ts` (functional `ApplicationConfig`, no `platformBrowserDynamic`/module bootstrap) |
| 6 | Covers all 5 PRD Feature areas (4.1–4.5) | **Pass**, with the caveat in Finding 2 (4.2's governing-AD list contains an unrelated AD) |
| 7 | No parent spine inherited (top/initiative altitude) | N/A per instructions — skipped |
| 8 | Every structural dimension initiative altitude should own is decided/deferred/open | **Pass**, with the minor caveat in Finding 5 (logging/observability silent, not explicitly bucketed) |

---

## Scaffold cross-checks performed

- `seed-b-backend.Api.csproj`: single `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` project, `net10.0`, `EntityFrameworkCore.SqlServer 10.0.11` → matches AD-1 and Stack table.
- `seed-b-backend.Api/Program.cs`: minimal hosting, no Controllers/Services/Data folders yet — consistent with (not contradicting) AD-1's target layering, since nothing has been built against it yet.
- `seed-b-backend.Tests/seed-b-backend.Tests.csproj`: `xunit.v3 3.2.2`, references the Api project → matches Stack table and Structural Seed's `seed-b-backend.Tests/` entry.
- `seed-b-frontend/package.json`: `@angular/core ^22.1.0`, `typescript ~6.0.2`, `vitest ^4.0.8`, `packageManager npm@11.17.0` → matches Stack table exactly.
- `seed-b-frontend/src/app/app.ts` + `app.config.ts`: standalone `@Component` with `imports: [RouterOutlet]`, functional `ApplicationConfig`/`provideRouter` — confirms AD-14's standalone-components mandate is already the scaffold's own default, not a change being imposed on it.
- `seed-b-backend.Api/Data/anfangsdatenbestand.json`: verified structure (`kategorien[].unterkategorien[].eigenschaften` as string-name list; `produkte[].eigenschaften` as typed-scalar object; `produkte[].angebote[]` as `{lieferantId, preis}` with **no id field**) — confirms AD-7's JSON-attribute design matches the source shape, and surfaces the AD-3 Offer-PK defect (Finding 1).
- `_bmad-output/.../addendum.md`: confirms Stack table entries were inherited from the mandate (not invented by the architecture step), and confirms the Deployment/Ops deferral is consistent with the addendum's own explicit non-goal.

---
title: Adversarial Review — Architecture Spine (Online-Handel Webshop)
target: architecture/architecture-bmad-core-bmm-2026-08-17/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md
method: builder-pair construction (two independent, spec-compliant implementers diverge)
created: 2026-08-17
---

# Adversarial Review — Architecture Spine

**Method.** For each candidate hole, I constructed two concrete, independent builders who each read only the spine (plus the PRD/addendum/seed file it binds to) and each obey every AD to the letter, then asked whether their outputs can still fail to interoperate. Findings below are only cases where the AD text genuinely underdetermines a *shared* contract (wire shape, schema field, query encoding) — not places where convention makes convergence overwhelmingly likely.

I additionally read the actual seed file (`seed-b-backend.Api/Data/anfangsdatenbestand.json`) because several holes only become visible against real data (e.g. `angebote[]` has no id field; `LeistungWatt` is an int, `KapazitaetLiter` a decimal-looking float, `KapazitaetLiter` is `null` on P10).

---

## Finding 1 — `Offer` has no business code in the seed, so AD-3 + AD-4's `offerId`/`supplierId` wording forks the checkout payload shape

**Severity: High — breaks the FE/BE wire contract for the single most important endpoint (`POST /api/orders`).**

AD-3's Rule states: *"`Category`, `Subcategory`, `Supplier`, `Product`, `Offer` keep the seed's string business codes... as primary key, unchanged from `anfangsdatenbestand.json`."*

But the seed has no such code for `Offer`. Each product's `angebote[]` entry is `{ "lieferantId": "L1", "preis": 29.99 }` — no `id` field at all. AD-3 asserts a premise ("Offer has a seed string code") that is false for this entity.

AD-4 then compounds it by describing the client cart line as holding `productId`, **`offerId`/`supplierId`** (the slash reads as "pick one representation") and `quantity` — without saying which.

**Builder A** (backend-first reading of AD-3 literally): gives `Offer` a synthetic single-column string PK (e.g. `"P1-L1"` generated at seed time, or a GUID), so it *does* have "a" business code to satisfy AD-3. The cart/checkout DTO then carries a single opaque `offerId: string`.

**Builder B** (reads AD-6's phrase *"every referenced product+supplier `Offer` still exists"* and the ER diagram's `PRODUCT ||--o{ OFFER`, `SUPPLIER ||--o{ OFFER` as the intended lookup key): models `Offer` as a pure composite-key junction row `(ProductId, SupplierId)` with no own id column at all. The cart/checkout DTO then carries `productId: string` + `supplierId: string`, no `offerId` field ever exists.

Both are fully AD-3/AD-4-compliant readings. The resulting `POST /api/orders` request bodies are structurally different (`{ productId, offerId, quantity }` vs `{ productId, supplierId, quantity }`), and a frontend built against one shape 500s or silently mis-references offers against a backend built to the other.

**Fix direction:** AD-3 should explicitly carve out `Offer` as the one exception — state it has *no* independent business code and is addressed only by the `(ProductId, SupplierId)` pair — or mint an explicit synthetic id convention (e.g. `"{ProductId}-{SupplierId}"`) and pin *that* as the wire field name. Either way, AD-4 (or a new AD) should give the literal JSON shape of the cart-line/checkout-item object, not a parenthetical field list with a `/` in it.

---

## Finding 2 — AD-5's field list vs. the structural note's "informational reference" disagree on whether `OrderItem` carries any Product/Supplier id at all

**Severity: Medium-High — changes both the DB schema and the order-confirmation response DTO.**

AD-5's Rule: *"`OrderItem` stores a complete denormalized copy at creation time — **product name, supplier name, unit price, quantity**. It never joins back to live `Product`/`Offer` rows for display."* No id field is listed.

The Structural Seed's ER diagram note directly under it says: *"`ORDER_ITEM` intentionally has no FK-drawn relationship to `PRODUCT`/`SUPPLIER` beyond **an informational reference** — it is a snapshot per AD-5, not a live join."* This implies some id-shaped field *does* exist, just without a DB foreign key.

**Builder A** implements AD-5's Rule literally: `OrderItem { ProductName, SupplierName, UnitPrice, Quantity }` — no `ProductId`/`SupplierId` columns anywhere, because none are listed.

**Builder B** implements the ER-diagram note literally: adds plain (non-FK-constrained) `ProductId string` / `SupplierId string` columns "for informational reference," matching AD-3's string-code types.

These produce different `OrderItem` schemas and, more importantly, different `GET /api/orders/{id}` response shapes: Builder B's confirmation page can carry a "view this product again" link (`productId` present); Builder A's cannot even if a later story wants one, because the snapshot literally never captured it. Two teams building the checkout confirmation UI against these two backends would diverge on what fields they can render/link.

**Fix direction:** Make AD-5's field list exhaustive and explicit about ids — either "OrderItem stores no product/supplier id, by design, to keep it a pure text snapshot" or add `ProductId`/`SupplierId` (typed as the string codes from AD-3, no FK constraint) to the enumerated field list.

---

## Finding 3 — Numeric-attribute JSON text-representation isn't pinned between what's stored (seed round-trip) and what a filter value is built as (AD-7)

**Severity: Medium — silent, not a crash: filters return zero results instead of erroring.**

AD-7's Rule does equality filtering via `JSON_VALUE` compared "as text for every value type incl. bool/number," with an explicit assumption flag that this is deliberately naive. The seed already contains attributes like `"KapazitaetLiter": 1.5` (P8), `"LeistungWatt": 900` (int-shaped), and `"KapazitaetLiter": null` (P10) — i.e. real non-string, non-trivially-formatted values that this filter has to match against exactly as text.

Nothing in AD-7 (or anywhere else in the spine) pins *how* a numeric attribute's filter value gets serialized on the wire, nor guarantees it matches how the stored JSON text renders that same number.

**Builder A (backend):** seeds `Product.Attributes` by deserializing the source JSON via `JsonDocument`/`JsonElement` and copying the raw token text through unchanged, so the column literally contains `1.5`, `900`, etc., verbatim from the seed file. `JSON_VALUE(Attributes, '$.KapazitaetLiter')` therefore returns the string `"1.5"`.

**Builder B (frontend):** builds the attribute-filter UI generically for "any numeric attribute" and, for display/input consistency with money fields elsewhere (AD-11 mandates `decimal` everywhere for money — a plausible team convention bleeds into "always show 2 decimals for numbers"), formats the filter value through a `decimal`-style pipe before sending it as a query param: `1.50` instead of `1.5`.

Result: `JSON_VALUE` returns `"1.5"`, the filter query param is `"1.50"`, the string-equality comparison in AD-7 fails, and the product silently disappears from filtered results — with no error, since AD-7's contract is "exact text equality," which is textually satisfied by rejecting the match. Both builders followed their AD to the letter; the interaction between "store raw seed text" and "format like money" is what breaks it.

**Fix direction:** AD-7 should pin a canonical text-serialization rule for numeric attribute values used in filtering (e.g. "filter values are compared using `TRY_CONVERT(decimal(18,4), ...)` for anything the Subcategory schema marks numeric, never raw string equality" — or simpler: mandate that filter options are only ever round-tripped from a `GET` of the distinct existing values, never freehand-typed or independently formatted by the client).

---

## Finding 4 — The wire encoding for dynamic, per-Subcategory attribute filters (AD-6/AD-7/AD-10) is entirely unspecified

**Severity: Medium — a functional gap, not just cosmetic: default ASP.NET Core model binding won't recover unknown query keys without an explicit binder.**

AD-10 establishes *that* filtering, search, sort, and paging are one server-side pipeline and the response carries paged items + total count — but no AD anywhere gives the actual `GET /api/products` query-string contract. Static params (`page`, `sortBy`) are conventional enough that two builders would likely converge unprompted, so per the task's own instruction I'm not flagging those. But the *attribute* filters (FR-6) are structurally different: their key names are **data**, not code — `Bauform`, `Kabellos`, `LeistungWatt`, `KapazitaetLiter`, `Verpackungsgroesse`, `Duft`, one set per Subcategory, defined only in the seed file. There is no single obvious convention for putting an open, subcategory-dependent set of key/value pairs on a query string, and — critically — ASP.NET Core's default model binder does **not** automatically capture arbitrary/unknown query keys into a `Dictionary<string,string>` without an explicit `[FromQuery]` binder wired for exactly that shape.

**Builder A (frontend):** sends filters as bare query keys matching the attribute name directly: `GET /api/products?unterkategorieId=K2a&LeistungWatt=900&KapazitaetLiter=1.5`.

**Builder B (backend):** defines the products endpoint's query DTO with an explicit `[FromQuery] Dictionary<string,string> filters` parameter, which ASP.NET Core can only populate from `?filters[LeistungWatt]=900&filters[KapazitaetLiter]=1.5` bracket notation — or alternatively expects a single JSON-encoded `?attributes={"LeistungWatt":"900"}` blob param.

Both builders followed AD-10 ("filters... execute as one server-side query pipeline") to the letter. Neither shape matches the other; filters silently never apply (attribute keys not recognized by the binder are just ignored, no error), which is exactly the kind of soft failure this project's own AD-7 assumption already flags as an accepted risk *for a different reason* — this compounds it with a second, purely contractual failure mode.

**Fix direction:** Add (or fold into AD-10) one explicit example query string showing the exact attribute-filter encoding, and state the products-list response envelope's field names (`items`/`totalCount`/`page` or equivalent) so both sides are building against the same literal contract, not a paraphrase of one.

---

## Finding 5 — AD-8 closes the *data* race (no duplicate rows) but not the *client-visible outcome* race for a genuinely concurrent first-time rating

**Severity: Low — internal to one Service, doesn't fork into two incompatible builders in the way 1-4 do, but is a real unclosed edge in the stated Rule.**

AD-8's Rule: *"a unique DB constraint on (`ProductId`, `AuthorName`) backs an upsert (update-if-exists else insert) for FR-10 — never check-then-insert at the app layer alone."* This does correctly prevent two rows for the same author/product ever existing, closing the data-integrity race. But it does not specify what happens to the losing request in the following interleaving:

1. Two `POST` requests for the same never-before-seen `(ProductId, AuthorName)` arrive concurrently (e.g. a double-submit from a slow network + retry, or two tabs).
2. Both check "does a row exist?" → no → both attempt `INSERT`.
3. The unique constraint lets exactly one `INSERT` through; the second raises a unique-violation.

AD-8 doesn't say whether the app layer is required to catch that violation and transparently retry as an `UPDATE` (returning 200 with a merged/second-writer-wins outcome), or whether it's acceptable to let it surface as an unhandled exception → generic 500 `ProblemDetails` via AD-12's global error handling. A builder who implements the upsert via a single atomic `MERGE` statement never hits this path at all; a builder who implements it via ORM-level "try insert, catch, then update" (a common, otherwise-correct EF Core pattern) will, under this specific race, occasionally return a 500 to a client who did nothing wrong. This isn't a cross-builder incompatibility (RatingService has one owner), but it is a Rule that reads as "closed" and isn't fully, and would benefit from one added sentence.

**Fix direction:** Add to AD-8: "a unique-constraint violation during the insert branch is caught and retried as an update, never surfaced to the client as an error."

---

## Non-findings (considered, ruled out)

- **AD-9 view-counter race** — genuinely closed; single atomic `UPDATE...SET x = x+1` has no lost-update window, and FR-9's own assumption already says no dedup is wanted, so repeated/duplicate GETs incrementing repeatedly is by design, not a bug.
- **AD-7 case-sensitivity of `JSON_VALUE` vs. AD-10's full-text search** — theoretically two different case-sensitivity behaviors, but in practice both run under SQL Server's default column collation (case-insensitive for the standard `SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS`-family collations), and filter *options* are realistically always populated by reading back existing distinct values rather than freehand-typed, so a real mismatch would require an additional, separately-flagged design choice (see Finding 3, which covers the more concrete numeric-formatting variant of this same category).
- **Client-submitted price on checkout** — checked whether a builder might trust a client-sent price for the `OrderItem` snapshot instead of re-deriving it server-side from the live `Offer`. AD-4's cart-line field list (`productId`, `offerId`/`supplierId`, `quantity`) does *not* include a price field, and the Design Paradigm's "client is never trusted with anything beyond display and input collection" statement is explicit. This loophole is already closed by the spine as written.
- **Exact HTTP verbs/routes for `GET /api/products`, `GET /api/products/{id}`, `GET /api/orders/{id}`** — REST-conventional enough (plural resource + id) that two independent builders converge without material incompatibility, per the task's own exclusion criterion. Flagged separately in Finding 4 only where the *query-string* shape (not the route) is the actual point of divergence.

---

## Summary Table

| # | AD(s) | Gap | Two builders diverge on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | AD-3, AD-4 | `Offer` has no seed business code; AD-4 writes `offerId`/`supplierId` as alternatives | Checkout request line shape: `offerId` vs `productId`+`supplierId` |
| 2 | AD-5, structural ER note | Field list vs. "informational reference" wording disagree | Whether `OrderItem` carries any Product/Supplier id at all |
| 3 | AD-7 | No canonical numeric-to-text rule for JSON attribute filter values | `"1.5"` (stored) vs `"1.50"` (client-formatted) never match |
| 4 | AD-6/7/10 | No pinned query-string encoding for dynamic per-subcategory attribute filters | Bare keys vs. bracket notation vs. JSON blob — filters silently no-op |
| 5 | AD-8 | Rule closes duplicate-row race, not the losing request's HTTP outcome | Silent-retry-as-update vs. surfaced 500 on concurrent first-time rating |

# Architecture Spine — Online-Handel Webshop

## Design Paradigm

Layered architecture (n-tier) inside the single existing ASP.NET Core project, paired with a separate Angular SPA client that consumes it over REST/JSON. **Server-authoritative**: there is no authentication anywhere in this system, so every trust-sensitive rule — price freezing, order validation, rating upsert, view counting — must live in backend Services; the client is never trusted with anything beyond display and input collection.

Layers map to folders inside `seed-b-backend.Api/`:

- **Controllers** (Presentation) — HTTP only, map DTOs to/from Service calls, no business logic.
- **Services** (Application) — all business rules: catalog querying, order validation and creation, rating upsert, view-count increment.
- **Data** (Persistence) — EF Core entities, `DbContext`, Migrations, startup seeding.

The Angular SPA (`seed-b-frontend/`) is a separate presentation-tier client with no business rules of its own beyond input validation for UX responsiveness — every rule it enforces client-side is re-enforced server-side.

## Invariants & Rules

### AD-1 — Backend internal layering & dependency direction

- **Binds:** all backend FRs (all of FR-1..FR-16)
- **Prevents:** business rules leaking into Controllers or EF entities; a future story splitting the solution into extra class-library projects that the existing single-project scaffold doesn't have
- **Rule:** `seed-b-backend.Api` stays one project, layered by folder as in Design Paradigm. Controllers never construct or query `DbContext` directly — only Services do. The frontend and any test project depend only on Controllers (via HTTP or, for tests, Services); nothing depends on Data except Services.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  FE["Angular SPA (seed-b-frontend)"] -->|HTTP/JSON only| Controllers
  Controllers --> Services
  Services --> Data["Data (EF Core entities, DbContext, Migrations)"]
  Data --> Db[("SQL Server")]
```

### AD-2 — English identifiers, German UI text

- **Binds:** all entities, DTOs, API routes, TS models
- **Prevents:** one story naming a class `Produkt`/route `/api/produkte` and another naming it `Product`/`/api/products`, splitting the codebase's vocabulary
- **Rule:** every code identifier (C# classes/EF entities, TS interfaces, API routes) uses the English noun below; all user-facing text stays German. Fixed mapping:

| German (PRD) | Code identifier |
| --- | --- |
| Kategorie | `Category` |
| Unterkategorie | `Subcategory` |
| Eigenschaft | `Attribute` |
| Produkt | `Product` |
| Lieferant | `Supplier` |
| Angebot | `Offer` |
| Warenkorb(-position) | `Cart`/`CartItem` (client-side only, AD-4) |
| Bestellung / Bestellposition | `Order` / `OrderItem` |
| Bewertung | `Rating` |
| Aufrufzähler | `ViewCount` |

### AD-3 — ID strategy

- **Binds:** FR-16 (seeding), FR-13/FR-14 (order), FR-10 (rating)
- **Prevents:** a story giving `Product` a surrogate int identity (breaking idempotent seed-matching by natural key) while another keeps the seed's string codes
- **Rule:** `Category`, `Subcategory`, `Supplier`, `Product`, `Offer` keep the seed's string business codes (`"K1"`, `"K1a"`, `"P1"`, `"L1"`, ...) as primary key, unchanged from `anfangsdatenbestand.json`. `Order`, `OrderItem`, `Rating` — entities created at runtime, not present in the seed — use server-generated GUID keys.

### AD-4 — Cart is client-side-only state

- **Binds:** FR-11, FR-12, FR-13
- **Prevents:** a server-side session/cookie mechanism that duplicates and can drift from frontend state
- **Rule:** there is no `Cart`/`CartItem` table, entity, or anonymous-session identity anywhere in the backend. The Angular app holds cart lines (`productId`, `offerId`/`supplierId`, `quantity`) in memory and in browser `localStorage` only. This is required by FR-12 itself: the cart must always display the *current* live offer price, not one captured at add-time, so a server-persisted cart copy would add nothing but staleness risk. Checkout (`POST /api/orders`) submits the full cart content plus delivery/contact data in one request.

### AD-5 — Order-time full snapshot

- **Binds:** FR-13, FR-14
- **Prevents:** any code path re-deriving an order line's displayed name/price from current catalog state, silently breaking the price-freeze guarantee when a supplier changes its price or the catalog is reseeded
- **Rule:** `OrderItem` stores a complete denormalized copy at creation time — product name, supplier name, unit price, quantity. It never joins back to live `Product`/`Offer` rows for display.

### AD-6 — Atomic order validation

- **Binds:** FR-13, FR-14, FR-15
- **Prevents:** an implementation that loops over cart lines and best-effort-inserts the valid ones, producing a partial order
- **Rule:** `POST /api/orders` validates the *entire* submitted cart — non-empty; every quantity is a positive integer; every referenced product+supplier `Offer` still exists — inside one Service method/DB transaction, before writing any `Order`/`OrderItem` row. Any single violation rejects the whole request (ProblemDetails, AD-12) with zero rows persisted and the client's cart left untouched. After creation, an order is retrievable only by the returned `OrderId` (confirmation page / direct link) — there is no listing or search endpoint, per the PRD's inherited assumption that order history stays outside this system's scope (open question, PRD OQ-1).

### AD-7 — Category-specific attributes as JSON

- **Binds:** FR-6, FR-8, FR-16
- **Prevents:** an EAV-table design in one story and a flat-columns-per-attribute design in another, producing incompatible schemas and incompatible filter queries
- **Rule:** `Product.Attributes` is stored as one JSON column matching the seed's per-product `eigenschaften` object 1:1 (typed scalars: string/bool/number/null). `Subcategory` owns the attribute-*name* schema (the list of names from `unterkategorien[].eigenschaften`) as its own small table/collection — values live only on `Product`. Filtering (FR-6) does exact-match equality against `JSON_VALUE` per requested attribute, AND-combined across attributes `[ASSUMPTION: equality compares the JSON scalar as text for every value type incl. bool/number — sufficient at this project's scale (14 seed products); no type-aware indexing]`.

### AD-8 — Rating integrity

- **Binds:** FR-10, FR-8
- **Prevents:** a stale denormalized average drifting from the underlying `Rating` rows if an update path is missed
- **Rule:** a unique DB constraint on (`ProductId`, `AuthorName`) backs an upsert (update-if-exists else insert) for FR-10 — never check-then-insert at the app layer alone. Average rating and rating count are always computed at **read time** via an aggregation query over `Rating` rows; they are never stored as denormalized columns on `Product`.

### AD-9 — View counter integrity

- **Binds:** FR-9, FR-7
- **Prevents:** lost updates under concurrent detail requests for the same product
- **Rule:** `Product.ViewCount` is a persisted column, incremented via a single atomic `UPDATE ... SET ViewCount = ViewCount + 1` on every product-detail `GET` — never a read-modify-write from the app layer.

### AD-10 — Server-side-only list querying

- **Binds:** FR-1 through FR-7
- **Prevents:** a frontend feature quietly re-sorting or re-paginating a page client-side and disagreeing with the backend's page/total-count metadata
- **Rule:** category/subcategory scope, full-text search, attribute filters, sort (name/price/popularity), and pagination all execute as **one** server-side query pipeline in the Product Service. The API response always carries the already-filtered/sorted/paged items plus total count; the Angular client never locally re-filters, re-sorts, or re-paginates a result set it already has.

### AD-11 — Money as decimal end-to-end

- **Binds:** FR-4 (price sort), FR-8, FR-9/FR-12/FR-13/FR-14 (totals)
- **Prevents:** floating-point rounding drift between cart-total, order-total, and per-line displays computed in different places
- **Rule:** all prices and sums use C# `decimal` / SQL `decimal(18,2)`. `float`/`double` are never used for currency, anywhere in the stack including Angular display formatting.

### AD-12 — Uniform API errors

- **Binds:** all endpoints
- **Prevents:** each controller inventing its own ad-hoc error JSON shape
- **Rule:** all API error responses — validation failures, FR-15 order rejection, not-found — use RFC7807 `ProblemDetails` (ASP.NET Core's built-in support), with a machine-readable reason per FR-15 case (`empty-cart` / `invalid-quantity` / `offer-unavailable`).

### AD-13 — Startup migrate-then-seed pipeline

- **Binds:** FR-16
- **Prevents:** relying on `EnsureCreated` (skips migrations), or an ad-hoc seed check scattered across multiple entry points that could reseed or duplicate data
- **Rule:** a single startup hook (hosted service) always applies pending EF Core migrations first, then seeds `anfangsdatenbestand.json` only if the `Product` table is empty, running once before the app accepts requests. This must be idempotent across repeated restarts with no intervening data deletion.

### AD-14 — Angular structure

- **Binds:** all frontend FRs
- **Prevents:** mixed NgModule/standalone styles, and components bypassing the shared API-client layer with ad-hoc `HttpClient` calls
- **Rule:** standalone components only (no NgModules), feature-folder layout (`core/` for shared HTTP services + models, `features/catalog`, `features/product-detail`, `features/cart`, `features/checkout`). Angular signals hold local reactive state (cart, active filters). Exactly one typed HTTP client service per backend resource; components never call `HttpClient` directly.

## Consistency Conventions

| Concern | Convention |
| --- | --- |
| Naming (entities, files, routes) | English identifiers everywhere in code (AD-2); routes follow `/api/` + plural English resource name, e.g. `/api/products`, `/api/orders` |
| Data & formats (ids, dates, money, errors) | string codes vs GUID per AD-3; dates ISO-8601 UTC; money as `decimal` (AD-11); errors as `ProblemDetails` (AD-12) |
| State & cross-cutting (mutation, auth) | no authentication anywhere (anonymous throughout); cart lives only in the browser (AD-4); every business rule lives in backend Services, never in Controllers or EF entity classes |

## Stack

| Name | Version |
| --- | --- |
| Angular | 22.1 |
| TypeScript | 6.0 |
| Node.js | 24.19 LTS |
| npm | (bundled with Node 24.19; workspace pins `packageManager: npm@11.17.0`) |
| ASP.NET Core | 10.0 |
| C# | 14 |
| .NET | 10.0 |
| Entity Framework Core (SqlServer provider) | 10.0.11 (as pinned in `seed-b-backend.Api.csproj`) |
| Microsoft SQL Server | (version supplied at runtime via `ConnectionStrings__Default`) |
| xUnit | v3 (backend tests) |
| Vitest | 4.0.8 (frontend tests, via `@angular/build`'s Vitest builder) |

## Structural Seed

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Browser["Angular SPA (Browser)"] -->|REST/JSON over HTTP| Api["ASP.NET Core Web API\n(seed-b-backend.Api)"]
  Api -->|EF Core| Db[("SQL Server")]
  Api -.->|reads once at startup, only if empty| Seed["anfangsdatenbestand.json"]
```

```mermaid
erDiagram
  CATEGORY ||--o{ SUBCATEGORY : has
  SUBCATEGORY ||--o{ PRODUCT : has
  SUBCATEGORY ||--o{ ATTRIBUTE_NAME : defines
  PRODUCT ||--o{ OFFER : "offered as"
  SUPPLIER ||--o{ OFFER : provides
  PRODUCT ||--o{ RATING : receives
  ORDER ||--|{ ORDER_ITEM : contains
```
*(`ORDER_ITEM` intentionally has no FK-drawn relationship to `PRODUCT`/`SUPPLIER` beyond an informational reference — it is a snapshot per AD-5, not a live join.)*

```text
seed-b-backend.Api/
  Controllers/           # thin HTTP endpoints, map DTO <-> Service
  Services/               # all business rules (catalog query, order validate+create, rating upsert, view count)
  Data/
    Entities/              # EF Core entity classes (Category, Subcategory, Product, Supplier, Offer, Order, OrderItem, Rating)
    AppDbContext.cs
    Migrations/
    Seeding/                # startup hosted service: migrate, then conditional seed from anfangsdatenbestand.json
  Dtos/                    # request/response contracts — Controllers never expose entities directly
seed-b-backend.Tests/
  ...                      # xUnit v3, mirrors Services/ (order validation, rating upsert, view count, price freeze)
seed-b-frontend/src/app/
  core/                    # shared typed HTTP client services, interceptors, models
  features/
    catalog/                # product list, category nav, search, filters, sort
    product-detail/         # detail view + rating form
    cart/                   # client-side cart store (signals + localStorage) + view
    checkout/                # order form + confirmation
```

## Capability → Architecture Map

| Capability / Area | Lives in | Governed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4.1 Produktkatalog (FR-1..FR-7) | `Services/ProductQueryService`, `Controllers/ProductsController`, `features/catalog` | AD-1, AD-7, AD-9, AD-10, AD-11 |
| 4.2 Produktdetail & Bewertungen (FR-8..FR-10) | `Services/ProductService`, `Services/RatingService`, `features/product-detail` | AD-5, AD-8, AD-9, AD-11 |
| 4.3 Warenkorb (FR-11, FR-12) | `features/cart` (Angular only — no backend entity) | AD-4, AD-11 |
| 4.4 Bestellung (FR-13..FR-15) | `Services/OrderService`, `Controllers/OrdersController`, `features/checkout` | AD-3, AD-5, AD-6, AD-11, AD-12 |
| 4.5 Anfangsdatenbestand (FR-16) | `Data/Seeding` | AD-3, AD-13 |

## Deferred

- **Product images (PRD OQ-2)** — no image/URL field in this spine; still open at PM level, revisit if resolved.
- **Quantity/order-value caps (PRD OQ-3)** — FR-15 fixes only "positive integer"; no upper bound designed.
- **Delivery-time hint on confirmation (PRD OQ-4)** — not modeled; `Order` carries no shipping-estimate field.
- **Order history / account-bound retrieval (PRD OQ-1)** — resolved for v1 by AD-6 (confirmation-link-only access); revisit if a later version needs it — would add an identity/session dimension this spine deliberately avoids (AD-4).
- **Supplier CRUD, sortiment/status admin area** — explicit PRD non-goals; `Supplier` and `Offer` stay read-only reference data sourced only from the seed file.
- **Deployment, containerization, operations** — explicit addendum non-goal; only the runtime contract (`ConnectionStrings__Default` env var) is fixed, nothing about hosting/infra/CI.
- **Caching and indexing strategy beyond EF Core defaults** — premature at seed scale (14 products); revisit if the product catalog grows materially.
- **API versioning** — single consumer (the bundled SPA), not needed for v1.
- **CORS/local-dev proxy configuration specifics** — needed to run frontend and backend together locally but is an implementation detail, not a divergence risk worth fixing here.

The API response always carries the already-filtered/sorted/paged items plus total count; the Angular client never locally re-filters, re-sorts, or re-paginates a result set it already has.

### AD-11 — Money as decimal end-to-end

- **Binds:** FR-4 (price sort), FR-8, FR-9/FR-12/FR-13/FR-14 (totals)
- **Prevents:** floating-point rounding drift between cart-total, order-total, and per-line displays computed in different places
- **Rule:** all prices and sums use C# `decimal` / SQL `decimal(18,2)`. `float`/`double` are never used for currency, anywhere in the stack including Angular display formatting.

### AD-12 — Uniform API errors

- **Binds:** all endpoints
- **Prevents:** each controller inventing its own ad-hoc error JSON shape
- **Rule:** all API error responses — validation failures, FR-15 order rejection, not-found — use RFC7807 `ProblemDetails` (ASP.NET Core's built-in support), with a machine-readable reason per FR-15 case (`empty-cart` / `invalid-quantity` / `offer-unavailable`).

### AD-13 — Startup migrate-then-seed pipeline

- **Binds:** FR-16
- **Prevents:** relying on `EnsureCreated` (skips migrations), or an ad-hoc seed check scattered across multiple entry points that could reseed or duplicate data
- **Rule:** a single startup hook (hosted service) always applies pending EF Core migrations first, then seeds `anfangsdatenbestand.json` only if the `Product` table is empty, running once before the app accepts requests. This must be idempotent across repeated restarts with no intervening data deletion.

### AD-14 — Angular structure

- **Binds:** all frontend FRs
- **Prevents:** mixed NgModule/standalone styles, and components bypassing the shared API-client layer with ad-hoc `HttpClient` calls
- **Rule:** standalone components only (no NgModules), feature-folder layout (`core/` for shared HTTP services + models, `features/catalog`, `features/product-detail`, `features/cart`, `features/checkout`). # Architecture Spine — Online-Handel Webshop

## Design Paradigm

Layered architecture (n-tier) inside the single existing ASP.NET Core project, paired with a separate Angular SPA client that consumes it over REST/JSON. **Server-authoritative**: there is no authentication anywhere in this system, so every trust-sensitive rule — price freezing, order validation, rating upsert, view counting — must live in backend Services; the client is never trusted with anything beyond display and input collection.

Layers map to folders inside `seed-b-backend.Api/`:

- **Controllers** (Presentation) — HTTP only, map DTOs to/from Service calls, no business logic.
- **Services** (Application) — all business rules: catalog querying, order validation and creation, rating upsert, view-count increment.
- **Data** (Persistence) — EF Core entities, `DbContext`, Migrations, startup seeding.

The Angular SPA (`seed-b-frontend/`) is a separate presentation-tier client with no business rules of its own beyond input validation for UX responsiveness — every rule it enforces client-side is re-enforced server-side.

## Invariants & Rules

### AD-1 — Backend internal layering & dependency direction

- **Binds:** all backend FRs (all of FR-1..FR-16)
- **Prevents:** business rules leaking into Controllers or EF entities; a future story splitting the solution into extra class-library projects that the existing single-project scaffold doesn't have
- **Rule:** `seed-b-backend.Api` stays one project, layered by folder as in Design Paradigm. Controllers never construct or query `DbContext` directly, and contain no conditional business logic (validation branching, price/total computation, aggregation) — a Controller action does DTO mapping and exactly one Service call, nothing else. The frontend and any test project depend only on Controllers (via HTTP or, for tests, Services); nothing depends on Data except Services.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  FE["Angular SPA (seed-b-frontend)"] -->|HTTP/JSON only| Controllers
  Controllers --> Services
  Services --> Data["Data (EF Core entities, DbContext, Migrations)"]
  Data --> Db[("SQL Server")]
```

### AD-2 — English identifiers, German UI text

- **Binds:** all entities, DTOs, API routes, TS models
- **Prevents:** one story naming a class `Produkt`/route `/api/produkte` and another naming it `Product`/`/api/products`, splitting the codebase's vocabulary
- **Rule:** every code identifier (C# classes/EF entities, TS interfaces, API routes) uses the English noun below; all user-facing text stays German. Fixed mapping:

| German (PRD) | Code identifier |
| --- | --- |
| Kategorie | `Category` |
| Unterkategorie | `Subcategory` |
| Eigenschaft | `Attribute` |
| Produkt | `Product` |
| Lieferant | `Supplier` |
| Angebot | `Offer` |
| Warenkorb(-position) | `Cart`/`CartItem` (client-side only, AD-4) |
| Bestellung / Bestellposition | `Order` / `OrderItem` |
| Bewertung | `Rating` |
| Aufrufzähler | `ViewCount` |

### AD-3 — ID strategy

- **Binds:** FR-16 (seeding), FR-13/FR-14 (order), FR-10 (rating)
- **Prevents:** a story giving `Product` a surrogate int identity (breaking idempotent seed-matching by natural key) while another keeps the seed's string codes
- **Rule:** `Category`, `Subcategory`, `Supplier`, `Product` keep the seed's string business codes (`"K1"`, `"K1a"`, `"P1"`, `"L1"`, ...) as primary key, unchanged from `anfangsdatenbestand.json`. `Offer` has **no id of its own in the seed** (`produkte[].angebote[]` carries only `lieferantId`+`preis`, nested per product) — it is keyed by the composite `(ProductId, SupplierId)`, which also enforces the glossary rule "a supplier offers a product at most once" as a DB constraint for free, no separate uniqueness AD needed. `Order`, `OrderItem`, `Rating` — entities created at runtime, not present in the seed — use server-generated GUID keys.

### AD-4 — Cart is client-side-only state

- **Binds:** FR-11, FR-12, FR-13
- **Prevents:** a server-side session/cookie mechanism that duplicates and can drift from frontend state
- **Rule:** there is no `Cart`/`CartItem` table, entity, or anonymous-session identity anywhere in the backend. The Angular app holds cart lines (`productId`, `offerId`/`supplierId`, `quantity`) in memory and in browser `localStorage` only. This is required by FR-12 itself: the cart must always display the *current* live offer price, not one captured at add-time, so a server-persisted cart copy would add nothing but staleness risk. Checkout (`POST /api/orders`) submits the full cart content plus delivery/contact data in one request.

### AD-5 — Order-time full snapshot

- **Binds:** FR-13, FR-14
- **Prevents:** any code path re-deriving an order line's displayed name/price from current catalog state, silently breaking the price-freeze guarantee when a supplier changes its price or the catalog is reseeded
- **Rule:** `OrderItem` stores a complete denormalized copy at creation time — product name, supplier name, unit price, quantity. It never joins back to live `Product`/`Offer` rows for display.

### AD-6 — Atomic order validation

- **Binds:** FR-13, FR-14, FR-15
- **Prevents:** an implementation that loops over cart lines and best-effort-inserts the valid ones, producing a partial order
- **Rule:** `POST /api/orders` validates the *entire* submitted cart — non-empty; every quantity is a positive integer; every referenced product+supplier `Offer` still exists — inside one Service method/DB transaction, before writing any `Order`/`OrderItem` row. Any single violation rejects the whole request (ProblemDetails, AD-12) with zero rows persisted and the client's cart left untouched. After creation, an order is retrievable only by the returned `OrderId` (confirmation page / direct link) — there is no listing or search endpoint, per the PRD's inherited assumption that order history stays outside this system's scope (open question, PRD OQ-1).

### AD-7 — Category-specific attributes as JSON

- **Binds:** FR-6, FR-8, FR-16
- **Prevents:** an EAV-table design in one story and a flat-columns-per-attribute design in another, producing incompatible schemas and incompatible filter queries
- **Rule:** `Product.Attributes` is stored as one JSON column matching the seed's per-product `eigenschaften` object 1:1 (typed scalars: string/bool/number/null). `Subcategory` owns the attribute-*name* schema (the list of names from `unterkategorien[].eigenschaften`) as its own small table/collection — values live only on `Product`. Filtering (FR-6) does exact-match equality against `JSON_VALUE` per requested attribute, AND-combined across attributes `[ASSUMPTION: equality compares the JSON scalar as text for every value type incl. bool/number — sufficient at this project's scale (14 seed products); no type-aware indexing]`.

### AD-8 — Rating integrity

- **Binds:** FR-10, FR-8
- **Prevents:** a stale denormalized average drifting from the underlying `Rating` rows if an update path is missed
- **Rule:** a unique DB constraint on (`ProductId`, `AuthorName`) backs an upsert (update-if-exists else insert) for FR-10 — never check-then-insert at the app layer alone. Average rating and rating count are always computed at **read time** via an aggregation query over `Rating` rows; they are never stored as denormalized columns on `Product`.

### AD-9 — View counter integrity

- **Binds:** FR-9, FR-7
- **Prevents:** lost updates under concurrent detail requests for the same product
- **Rule:** `Product.ViewCount` is a persisted column, incremented via a single atomic `UPDATE ... SET ViewCount = ViewCount + 1` on every product-detail `GET` — never a read-modify-write from the app layer.

### AD-10 — Server-side-only list querying

- **Binds:** FR-1 through FR-7
- **Prevents:** a frontend feature quietly re-sorting or re-paginating a page client-side and disagreeing with the backend's page/total-count metadata
- **Rule:** category/subcategory scope, full-text search, attribute filters, sort (name/price/popularity), and pagination all execute as **one** server-side query pipeline in the Product Service. The API response always carries the already-filtered/sorted/paged items plus total count; the Angular client never locally re-filters, re-sorts, or re-paginates a result set it already has.

### AD-12 — Uniform API errors
